reason: The text emphasizes strict hierarchy throughout: God commands Abraham with absolute authority, Abraham immediately obeys ('Here I am'); Abraham commands his servants to stay behind and his son Isaac to accompany him; Isaac submits to his father's authority; the angel of the Lord (divine messenger) speaks with authority from heaven. The entire narrative centers on demonstrating Abraham's unwavering obedience to God's hierarchical command, even against his own will. Paternal authority over Isaac and servant authority relationships are also clearly established and respected. Hierarchy is not merely present—it is the structural and theological foundation of the passage.
